decision_semantics.KEEP: Keep this concept as-is for artwork creation/import. This is NOT artwork acceptance.
decision_semantics.EDIT: Keep the concept but revise copy/visual direction before artwork creation.
decision_semantics.REGEN: Keep the underlying idea but request a different visual/generation direction after artwork work begins.
decision_semantics.SKIP: Do not spend artwork effort on this concept now.

records.title: Avionics — technician black cloud
records.hook: I DON'T BREAK IT. I FIND WHAT WAS ALREADY BROKEN.
records.concept: Celebrate the tech who touches a simple job and discovers the much worse hidden problem.
records.purchase_reason: Defensive humor + competence pride for the 'black cloud' technician.
records.differentiation: The line is about perception and truth, not systems jargon.
records.profession_context: Avionics technicians inspect and troubleshoot aircraft electrical, electronic and computer-based systems, often tracing complicated faults through interconnected equipment and wiring.
records.joke_explanation: This is defensive technician humor: “I did not break it; I exposed what was already broken.” It celebrates the person who keeps finding hidden faults and then has to explain why the problem is now visible.
records.line_meaning: The technician investigates one job and uncovers a deeper pre-existing problem. From the outside it can look as though the technician caused the new problem simply because it was discovered while they were working.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Peers know the tech who always finds the deeper issue.
records.human_idea: The human premise is being blamed for revealing a pre-existing problem.
records.visual_direction: Storm cloud over a generic aircraft wiring bundle, with hidden fault revealed.
records.listing_title: Avionics Technician Black Cloud Humor T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: For avionics technicians who keep finding the fault that was already hiding there.
records.highlight_2: Dry troubleshooting humor for aircraft electrical and electronics maintenance crews.
records.description: Avionics workplace humor about uncovering the deeper fault and then having to explain that finding it did not cause it.

records.title: BMET — twenty-minute walk, thirty-second fix
records.concept: Celebrate the disproportion between the time spent getting to a call and the tiny fix itself.
records.purchase_reason: A concise work-story joke that a BMET can wear and another BMET can instantly validate.
records.differentiation: The value is the absurd ratio, not terminology.
records.profession_context: Biomedical equipment technicians install, maintain, calibrate and repair medical equipment throughout hospitals and other clinical facilities.
records.joke_explanation: The insider recognition is the ratio: a long trip through the building for a tiny fix. It is funny because the logistics can be more time-consuming than the technical problem.
records.line_meaning: The technician may spend much longer walking across a large hospital to reach a service call than the actual repair takes once they arrive.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Insider response should be 'that is exactly my day.'
records.human_idea: The human idea is spending far more effort reaching the problem than solving it.
records.visual_direction: Large 20:00 versus 0:30 typography with a small generic tool icon.
records.highlight_1: BMET humor for the service call where getting there takes longer than the repair.
records.highlight_2: Made for biomedical equipment technicians working across hospitals and clinical facilities.
records.description: A biomedical equipment technician joke about crossing the hospital for a repair that takes only seconds once you arrive.

records.title: Cytology — cells confess
records.hook: I STARE AT CELLS UNTIL ONE CONFESSES.
records.concept: Turn microscopic interpretation into a detective interrogation metaphor.
records.purchase_reason: Strong visual metaphor, identity humor and giftability.
records.differentiation: The hook is detective behavior, not cell terminology.
records.profession_context: Cytotechnologists examine prepared slides of body cells under a microscope and look for abnormalities that can signal disease, including cancerous changes.
records.joke_explanation: It turns patient, detail-heavy diagnostic work into a noir detective scene. The professional pride is that the cytotech is the person who notices the one abnormal cell hiding among many normal ones.
records.line_meaning: The line compares careful microscopic examination to a detective interrogation: stare long enough and one suspicious cell finally “confesses.”
records.expected_insider_reaction: Cytotechs recognize the long search for the one suspicious cell.
records.human_idea: The human premise is patient observation eventually revealing the culprit.
records.visual_direction: Microscope spotlight/interrogation room with stylized generic cells.
records.highlight_1: Microscope humor for cytotechnologists who patiently search until the suspicious cell stands out.
records.highlight_2: A detective-style lab joke without medical claims, patient imagery, or diagnostic promises.
records.description: Cytology workplace humor that turns careful microscopic examination into a detective interrogation scene.

records.title: Electronics tech — arguing with circuits
records.hook: I ARGUE WITH CIRCUITS UNTIL THEY ADMIT WHAT'S WRONG.
records.concept: Anthropomorphize diagnosis as an argument with a stubborn board.
records.target_buyer: Electrical/electronic engineering technicians and repair techs
records.purchase_reason: Humor + competence pride; strong visual and gifting potential.
records.differentiation: Human metaphor rather than component list.
records.profession_context: Electrical and electronics technicians troubleshoot circuits, boards and systems by measuring signals, tracing faults and testing possible causes.
records.joke_explanation: Anyone who troubleshoots stubborn electronics knows the feeling of negotiating with a machine that refuses to tell you what is wrong. The phrase turns diagnostic persistence into a human argument.
records.line_meaning: The circuit cannot talk. “Arguing” means repeatedly testing hypotheses until the measurements finally reveal the actual fault.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Repair techs recognize the stubborn back-and-forth of diagnosis.
records.human_idea: The human premise is persuading an uncooperative object to reveal the truth.
records.visual_direction: Technician speech bubble facing an annoyed circuit board character.
records.listing_title: Electronics Technician Arguing With Circuits T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: Troubleshooting humor for electronics technicians who keep testing until the circuit gives up the answer.
records.highlight_2: For bench techs, repair techs, and anyone who has negotiated with stubborn electronics.
records.description: Electronics technician humor about the familiar back-and-forth of testing, measuring, and tracing a stubborn fault.

records.title: I&C — what instrument do you play
records.hook: ASKED WHAT INSTRUMENT I PLAY. I SAID 4–20 mA.
records.concept: Use the recurring outsider misunderstanding of 'instrument technician' as the setup.
records.purchase_reason: Actual joke with outsider setup and insider punchline; highly giftable.
records.differentiation: Technical term functions as a punchline, not a list.
records.profession_context: Instrumentation & Controls technicians work with sensors, transmitters, control loops and industrial process signals. A common analog signal standard is 4–20 mA.
records.joke_explanation: It is a double-meaning joke: “instrument” means one thing to the public and something different in process control. I&C people instantly recognize 4–20 mA, so the punchline doubles as an insider badge.
records.line_meaning: An outsider hears “instrument technician” and thinks musical instrument. The technician answers with “4–20 mA,” treating an industrial current-loop signal as if it were the instrument they play.
records.expected_insider_reaction: I&C techs laugh because they have been asked the setup question.
records.human_idea: The human premise is someone misunderstanding your profession as a musical one.
records.visual_direction: Concert-poster layout with a process signal replacing a musical waveform.
records.highlight_1: An instrumentation and controls joke built around the 4–20 mA signal every I&C tech recognizes.
records.highlight_2: For technicians working with sensors, transmitters, process signals, and control loops.
records.description: I&C insider humor using the double meaning of “instrument” and the familiar 4–20 mA industrial signal.

records.title: Relay tech — one click, large meeting
records.hook: ONE CLICK AWAY FROM A VERY LARGE MEETING.
records.concept: Gallows humor about the organizational consequences of one wrong action.
records.purchase_reason: Memorable high-consequence workplace humor with strong coworker gift appeal.
records.differentiation: No technical list; the joke is consequence disproportion.
records.profession_context: Substation / relay technicians test and maintain protection systems that detect electrical faults and can command circuit breakers to trip. Their work is high-consequence: a small configuration or switching mistake can affect major equipment and operations.
records.joke_explanation: The humor is the absurd mismatch between the size of the action and the size of the organizational fallout. Relay technicians immediately understand why a seemingly small action can make everyone very interested very quickly.
records.line_meaning: The line says that one tiny click can create consequences big enough to trigger a serious incident review or a room full of people asking what happened.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Peers laugh because they understand exactly why the meeting would be large.
records.human_idea: The human premise is a tiny action causing enormous organizational consequences.
records.visual_direction: Tiny switch casting a huge conference-room shadow.
records.listing_title: Relay Technician One Click Large Meeting T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: Relay technician humor about a tiny action with consequences big enough to fill a meeting room.
records.highlight_2: For protection and substation technicians who know how quickly one click gets everyone's attention.
records.description: Protection and relay technician humor about the huge organizational consequences that can follow one small action.

records.title: Relay tech — professionally making people nervous
records.hook: TRIP TEST: PROFESSIONALLY MAKING PEOPLE NERVOUS.
records.concept: Humor about trip testing making everyone nearby tense even when done correctly.
records.differentiation: The concept centers other people's reaction, not test-step jargon.
records.profession_context: Protection / relay technicians test electrical protection schemes that are designed to issue trip commands when faults occur. Testing is done carefully because these systems interact with breakers and critical power equipment.
records.joke_explanation: The technician is calm because this is normal work; observers are tense because they understand the consequences if something happens unexpectedly. The humor is being professionally responsible for making the room nervous.
records.line_meaning: A trip test is routine professional work for the technician, but everyone nearby knows that “trip” is connected to opening breakers and taking equipment out of service.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Relay techs recognize how everyone watches during a trip test.
records.human_idea: The human premise is being calm while your routine work makes everyone else anxious.
records.visual_direction: Nervous observers behind a calm technician at a test set.
records.listing_title: Relay Technician Trip Test Humor T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: Trip-test humor for relay technicians who stay calm while everyone else watches a little more closely.
records.highlight_2: For protection, substation, and relay crews working around breakers and critical power equipment.
records.description: Relay technician workplace humor about routine trip testing and the nervous attention it can create around the room.

records.title: Fab tech — coffee versus gowning
records.hook: GOWN. UNGOWN. REGRET THE COFFEE. REPEAT.
records.concept: Cleanroom life joke about regretting fluids because every bathroom trip means ungowning and regowning.
records.purchase_reason: High-recognition cleanroom humor with broad wearability.
records.differentiation: The joke is human inconvenience, not wafer terminology.
records.profession_context: Semiconductor processing technicians work in cleanrooms where particle contamination must be controlled. Entering often requires a hood, cleanroom suit, gloves and other gowning steps; leaving reverses that process.
records.joke_explanation: The joke is that a completely normal choice — drinking coffee — creates an annoyingly elaborate chain of work. Fab workers recognize the daily calculation immediately: is the coffee worth having to do all that again?
records.line_meaning: Coffee eventually means a bathroom break. In a cleanroom, that can mean leaving the controlled area, ungowning, then repeating the gowning routine when you come back.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Fab workers immediately recognize the bathroom/coffee calculation.
records.human_idea: The human premise is a tiny daily choice causing an absurd routine.
records.visual_direction: Coffee cup caught in a loop diagram of gowning stages, stylized not procedural.
records.listing_title: Semiconductor Fab Tech Coffee Gowning Humor T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: Cleanroom humor for fab techs who know a simple coffee can turn into another full gowning cycle.
records.highlight_2: For semiconductor processing technicians living the gown, ungown, repeat routine.
records.description: Semiconductor fab humor about the daily cleanroom calculation: whether the coffee is worth doing the gowning routine again.

records.title: Fab tech — dust outranks me
records.hook: ONE SPECK OF DUST OUTRANKS ME.
records.concept: Personify contamination rules as a tiny speck having more authority than the worker.
records.purchase_reason: Visual humor and cleanroom identity with low jargon dependence.
records.differentiation: The premise is power/status inversion, not cleanroom terminology.
records.profession_context: Semiconductor cleanroom work is dominated by contamination control because tiny particles can damage sensitive fabrication processes.
records.joke_explanation: The absurdity is the power hierarchy: a nearly invisible particle “outranks” a human employee. It turns strict cleanroom discipline into a tiny manager character.
records.line_meaning: The technician jokes that a microscopic speck of dust has more authority than they do because contamination rules dictate what everyone can touch, wear and do.
records.expected_insider_reaction: Fab techs recognize how contamination rules dominate everything.
records.human_idea: The human premise is something tiny controlling your entire behavior.
records.visual_direction: Tiny dust particle wearing a manager badge above a suited technician.
records.listing_title: Semiconductor Fab Tech Dust Outranks Me T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: Cleanroom humor for semiconductor techs who know a microscopic particle can dictate the whole day.
records.highlight_2: A contamination-control workplace joke for fab, cleanroom, and semiconductor processing crews.
records.description: Semiconductor cleanroom humor about the absurd hierarchy where one tiny speck of dust can control everything.

records.title: SPD — one dirty instrument
records.hook: ONE OF YOU IS DIRTY. EVERYBODY GOES BACK.
records.concept: Make one dirty instrument the guilty classmate that sends the entire tray back.
records.purchase_reason: Strong inside joke plus standards pride; it is easy to gift to an SPD tech.
records.differentiation: The humor comes from collective punishment, not instrument names.
records.profession_context: Sterile Processing staff clean, inspect, package and sterilize reusable medical instruments so they are safe for the next patient.
records.joke_explanation: The line treats the instrument tray like a school class: one “dirty” member gets caught and everybody gets sent back. SPD workers recognize the frustration of one problem resetting work on a whole set.
records.line_meaning: If something in a set is still contaminated or otherwise fails inspection, the set cannot simply move forward as if everything were fine.
records.expected_insider_reaction: SPD peers recognize the pain of one item resetting the work.
records.human_idea: The premise is the familiar human comedy of one person's mistake sending the whole group back.
records.visual_direction: Cartoon tray lineup with one guilty-looking generic instrument; no gore.
records.listing_title: Sterile Processing One Dirty Instrument Humor T-Shirt
records.highlight_1: SPD humor for the moment one instrument fails inspection and the whole set has to go back.
records.highlight_2: For sterile processing technicians who clean, inspect, package, and sterilize reusable instruments.
records.description: Sterile Processing workplace humor about one problem resetting the work for an entire instrument set.
